info.name: Clutch
info.description:
Clutch is a distributed lock management platform. This collection exercises the full **v0.2.0 (alpha)** REST API: authentication, tenant / user / application-key administration, the complete lock lifecycle (acquire, heartbeat, release, force-release), observability (lock audit and request history), server settings, and the destructive tenant nuke.

## Getting started
The collection is self-contained — every variable (including `baseUrl` and the seeded dev key) lives on the collection, so there is no separate environment to import.
1. Import the collection.
2. Review the collection variables, most importantly `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:8080`, the Docker load balancer) and `accessKey` (the seeded dev application key).
3. Run **Auth → Login (application key)** first. It exchanges the access key for a bearer `token` and stores it as a collection variable; collection-level bearer auth then applies it to every other request automatically.
4. Run **Tenants → List tenants** to capture `tenantId`, then work through the tenant-scoped folders.

## Authentication
All requests except Health, the OpenAPI document, and Login require a bearer token. Log in with an application key (`{ accessKey }`) or with tenant user credentials (`{ tenantId, email, password }`). The application access key is the sole connect credential — Clutch never issues or accepts a separate secret key. Roles are system admin, tenant admin, and user; each request notes what it needs.

## Locks over REST *and* WebSocket
Locks can be acquired, renewed, and released over **both** this REST API (the **Locks** folder) and the WebSocket API (`WEBSOCKETS_API.md`) — the same lock engine backs both. The difference: a WebSocket holder is released automatically when the socket closes, whereas a **REST holder is not tied to a connection**. A REST hold lives entirely on its TTL lease — renew it with **Heartbeat** before `leaseExpiresUtc`, release it explicitly, or let the lease lapse and be swept. Renewal is bounded by the key's `maxHoldMs`, so a hold cannot be extended forever. Every grant returns a monotonic `fencingToken`; pass it to the resource you protect so a stale holder can be fenced off.

## Pagination
Every list endpoint uses a uniform EnumerationQuery / EnumerationResult contract. Pass `maxResults` (1–1000, default 25), `skip` (offset), and `ordering` (`CreatedDescending` default, `CreatedAscending`, `NameAscending`, `NameDescending`). The response is `{ success, maxResults, skip, totalRecords, recordsRemaining, endOfResults, timestampUtc, objects: [...] }`.

## Variables
`baseUrl`, `accessKey`, `token`, `tenantId`, `userId`, `credentialId`, `lockKey`, `sessionId`, `holderId`, `fencingToken`, `requestId` — captured automatically by the Login, List, Create, and Acquire requests as you run them.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Session-token lifecycle. **Login** exchanges an application key (or tenant user credentials) for the bearer token that collection-level auth applies to every other request. The token is short-lived (see `tokenLifetimeMinutes` in Server Settings) — re-run Login when it expires.

request.description: Anonymous entry point. Exchange an application access key for a session token. Body: `{ accessKey }` for an application key, or `{ tenantId, email, password }` to sign in as a tenant user instead. Returns `{ token, principalType, tenantId }`. Captures `token` and `tenantId` on success; an unknown or inactive key returns 401.
Resolve and return the principal context for the current bearer token (tenant, roles, principal name). Returns 401 if the token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked.
The decoded principal details for the current token — the same resolution as Validate token.
Revoke the current session token. Returns 204; authenticated calls fail with 401 afterward until you log in again.

item.name: System
item.description: Unauthenticated health and service metadata, plus the live OpenAPI document.

request.description: Anonymous liveness probe including database connectivity. Returns 200 when the node and its database are reachable; a degraded node returns a non-200.
Product, version, node id, database type, live WebSocket connection count, telemetry configuration, and the resolved principal. Requires a bearer token.
The server's live OpenAPI 3 document — the same spec that drives the dashboard's API Explorer. Anonymous.

item.name: Tenants
item.description:
Tenant administration. A tenant is an isolated namespace for locks, users, and application keys, each with its own lease and retention settings. A system administrator sees and manages every tenant; a tenant admin sees only their own.

Tenant shape: `{ id, name, lockHistoryRetentionDays, defaultLeaseMs, maxLeaseMs, active, isProtected, createdUtc, lastUpdateUtc }`.

request.description: Paginated list of tenants (EnumerationResult — see the collection overview for the pagination contract). A system admin sees all tenants; other principals see only their own. Query: `maxResults` (1–1000, default 25), `skip`, `ordering`. Captures the first tenant id into `tenantId`.

exec: if (pm.response.code===200){ const r=pm.response.json(); const a=(r&&r.objects)||[]; if(a.length){ pm.collectionVariables.set('tenantId', a[0].id);} }

request.description: System admin only. Body: `{ name, lockHistoryRetentionDays?, defaultLeaseMs?, maxLeaseMs? }` — omitted lock fields fall back to server defaults. Returns 201 with the created tenant.
Read a single tenant by id. Returns 404 if it does not exist or is out of the caller's scope.
System admin, or the tenant's own admin. The body mirrors create; supplied fields replace the current values. Returns the updated tenant.

System admin only. Deletes the tenant and cascades to its users, application keys, locks, lock definitions, lock audit, auth sessions, and request history. Protected tenants cannot be deleted. Returns 204. For a guarded, auditable purge with per-entity counts, use **Admin → Nuke tenant** instead.

item.name: Users
item.description: Tenant users authenticate with email + password (see Auth → Login). Scoped to `{{tenantId}}`: reads require tenant read access, writes require tenant admin (or system admin). Password hashes are never returned.

request.description: Paginated list of the tenant's users (EnumerationResult with `objects`). Query: `maxResults`, `skip`, `ordering`.
Tenant admin. Body: `{ email, password, firstName?, lastName?, isSystemAdmin?, isTenantAdmin?, active? }`. Only a system admin may set `isSystemAdmin`. Returns 201; captures `userId`.
Read a single user by id (password hash omitted).

Tenant admin. Supplied fields replace the current values. Include `password` only to change it (omit to keep the existing one). Only a system admin may change `isSystemAdmin`. Returns the updated user.
Delete a user and its application keys. Returns 204.

item.name: Credentials
item.description: Application keys are the credentials clients and automation use to authenticate (see Auth → Login with `accessKey`). Scoped to `{{tenantId}}`. The raw access key is returned only once, at creation; it is redacted everywhere else. Clutch issues no separate secret key.

request.description: Paginated list of application keys (EnumerationResult with `objects`); access keys are redacted. Query: `maxResults`, `skip`, `ordering`.
Tenant admin. Body: `{ name, userId?, expiresUtc? }`. Returns 201 with the one-time `accessKey` — the sole credential, there is no secret key. Captures `credentialId` and `accessKey`.

exec: if(pm.response.code===201){ const b=pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('credentialId', b.id); if(b.accessKey) pm.collectionVariables.set('accessKey', b.accessKey);}

request.description: Read a single application key (access key redacted).
Delete an application key. Clients still using it will fail to authenticate. Returns 204.

item.name: Locks
item.description:
The full lock lifecycle over REST — acquire, heartbeat, release, release-session, and admin force-release — plus live-state observability. These mirror the WebSocket frames of the same name and are backed by the same engine, but a **REST holder is not tied to a connection**: it lives on a TTL lease that you renew with **Heartbeat** before `leaseExpiresUtc`.

Run **Acquire lock** first; it captures `sessionId`, `holderId`, and `fencingToken` for the heartbeat/release requests. A lock key containing `/` must be URL-encoded in the path (for example `orders%2F42`).

Holder shape: `{ id, tenantId, lockKey, mode, credentialId, sessionId, nodeId, fencingToken, acquiredUtc, leaseExpiresUtc, lastHeartbeatUtc }`.

request.description: Paginated live holders (EnumerationResult with `objects`). Optional filters: `name` (key substring), `mode` (Read|Write|Delete). Pagination: `maxResults`, `skip`, `ordering`.
The lock definition and every current holder for `{{lockKey}}` — `{ definition, holders }`.

Acquire a lock on `{{lockKey}}`. Body: `{ mode, behavior?, timeoutMs?, leaseMs?, sessionId?, policy?, strictPolicy? }`.
- `mode`: Read | Write | Delete.
- `behavior`: `FailFast` (default — return immediately) or `Wait` (block up to `timeoutMs`, capped by the server's max wait).
- `leaseMs`: requested hold time, clamped to the key's max lease; renew before it expires with Heartbeat.
- `sessionId`: omit and the server assigns one (returned and captured); reuse it to group more holders.
- `policy` / `strictPolicy`: `policy` applies only when this caller first creates the key; on an existing key it is ignored unless `strictPolicy` is true, which rejects a conflicting policy.

Granted → **201** `{ result: "Granted", granted: true, key, mode, holderId, sessionId, fencingToken, leaseExpiresUtc }`. Not grantable → **409** `{ result: "Denied"|"Timeout"|"PolicyConflict", granted: false, key, sessionId, reason }`. Captures `sessionId`, `holderId`, and `fencingToken`.

Renew the leases of holders owned by `{{sessionId}}` before `leaseExpiresUtc`. Body: `{ holderIds: [ ... ] }`. Returns `{ sessionId, renewed: [ { holderId, leaseExpiresUtc } ] }`. A holder that has reached its key's `maxHoldMs` is not renewable and is omitted from `renewed` — heartbeat cannot extend a hold indefinitely.

Release one holder you own. Body: `{ holderId, sessionId }` — **both are required** and must match the values returned by Acquire. Idempotent: `released` is false (still 200) if the holder was already gone. Note: the WebSocket release needs only a holderId, but the REST release requires the sessionId too.
Release **every** holder owned by `{{sessionId}}` — the REST equivalent of a WebSocket disconnect. Returns `{ sessionId, released: [ holderId, ... ], count }`.
Tenant admin. Revoke every holder on `{{lockKey}}` regardless of session — an operator override. Returns `{ key, released }` (the number revoked).

item.name: Lock Audit
item.description: The append-only lock-lifecycle audit trail and the time-bucketed summary that powers the dashboard's Lock Activity chart. Retention is governed per tenant by `lockHistoryRetentionDays`.

request.description: Paginated audit entries (EnumerationResult with `objects`), newest first. Event types: `PolicyCreated`, `Acquired`, `Released`, `Waited`, `Denied`, `Expired`, `Revoked`, `HeartbeatRenewed`. Pagination: `maxResults`, `skip`, `ordering`; plus optional `name`, `mode`, `fromUtc`, `toUtc` filters.

Time-bucketed event counts grouped by **operation (event) type** over `[fromUtc, toUtc)`. Query: `bucketCount` (default 96), optional `name`, `mode`, `fromUtc`, `toUtc`. Returns `{ fromUtc, toUtc, bucketCount, bucketStartsUtc: [...], series: [ { label, counts: [...] } ] }` where each series `label` is an event type and each series is a stacked line/bar in the chart.

item.name: Request History
item.description: Captured API traffic for observability. Secret-bearing headers are redacted and bodies are truncated to a configurable size; retention is set in Server Settings. Tenant-scoped from the token; a system admin may widen scope with `tenantId`.

request.description: Paginated request list (EnumerationResult with `objects`; bodies omitted). Optional filters: `method`, `statusCode`, `pathContains`, `fromUtc`, `toUtc`, and (admin) `tenantId`, `userId`. Pagination: `maxResults`, `skip`, `ordering`. Captures the first entry id into `requestId`.

exec: if(pm.response.code===200){ const r=pm.response.json(); const a=(r&&r.objects)||[]; if(a.length){ pm.collectionVariables.set('requestId', a[0].id);} }

request.description: Time-bucketed success/failure counts and average durations for the request-activity chart. Query: `bucketMinutes` (default 15) plus the same filters as the list. Returns `{ totalCount, totalSuccess, totalFailure, averageDurationMs, buckets: [ { bucketStartUtc, bucketEndUtc, successCount, failureCount, averageDurationMs } ] }`.

Read one entry in full, including its redacted request/response headers and the (truncated) bodies. Set `requestId` from a List result (List captures the first automatically). 404 if not found or out of scope.
Delete a single request-history entry. Returns 204.

Delete every entry matching the filter (here `statusCode=404`). Returns `{ deletedCount }`. Supports the same filters as the list — sending it with no filters purges everything in scope, so use with care.

item.name: Server Settings
item.description: System-admin-only server configuration. Read the running settings, update them (which also rewrites the on-disk JSON file), and trigger a restart so changes that require one take effect. Secrets (auth signing key, admin API key, database password) are redacted as `***` on read and preserved on write when you send `***` back.

request.description: System admin. Return the full on-disk settings (camelCase; secrets redacted as `***`). Copy this response into **Update settings**, edit it, and PUT it back.

body.raw:
{
  "nodeId": "node1",
  "rest": { "hostname": "*", "port": 8080, "ssl": false },
  "database": { "type": "Postgresql", "host": "postgres", "port": 5432, "databaseName": "clutch", "username": "postgres", "password": "***", "maxPoolSize": 100 },
  "logging": { "consoleLogging": true, "fileLogging": false, "logDirectory": "./logs/", "logFilename": "clutch.log", "minimumSeverity": 1 },
  "auth": { "issuer": "clutch", "signingKey": "***", "tokenLifetimeMinutes": 60, "adminApiKey": "***" },
  "lock": { "defaultLeaseMs": 30000, "maxLeaseMs": 300000, "maxHoldMs": 3600000, "maxWaitMs": 60000, "waiterPollMs": 1000, "sweepIntervalMs": 1000 },
  "requestHistory": { "enabled": true, "maxRequestBodyBytes": 65536, "maxResponseBodyBytes": 65536, "retentionDays": 30 },
  "telemetry": { "enabled": true, "serviceName": "clutch", "prometheusEnable": false, "prometheusHostname": "*", "prometheusPort": 9464, "prometheusPath": "/metrics", "otlpEnable": true, "otlpEndpoint": "http://otel-collector:4317", "metricsIncludeRuntime": true, "metricsIncludeProcess": true },
  "mcp": { "enable": true, "hostname": "*", "port": 8100, "mcpPath": "/mcp", "serverName": "Clutch MCP" }
}

request.description: System admin. PUT the **complete** settings object returned by Get settings, with your edits — omitted sections are reset to defaults, so always send the whole object. Leave a secret as `***` to keep its current value. Returns `{ saved, restartRequired, message, settings }`. Most changes take effect only after a restart.

System admin. Ask the node to restart so pending settings take effect. Returns 202 `{ restarting, node }`; the process then exits and (under Docker's restart policy) relaunches with the updated settings. The current connection drops briefly.

System admin. Validate a database configuration without saving it. Send a database settings object (type is Postgresql, Mysql, SqlServer, or Sqlite); a blank or *** password reuses the running one. Returns { ok, message, provider }. The example tests a SQLite file; set host/port/databaseName/username/password for the networked providers.

item.name: Admin
item.description: System-admin-only destructive operations, guarded by explicit confirmation.

body.raw:
{
  "tenantId": "{{tenantId}}",
  "confirmTenantId": "{{tenantId}}",
  "reason": "Decommissioning the tenant per ticket OPS-1234.",
  "includeAuditRecords": true,
  "includeRequestHistory": true
}

request.description:
**Destructive — system admin only.** Permanently destroy `{{tenantId}}` and every record scoped to it (users, application keys, locks, lock definitions, lock audit, auth sessions, and — when included — request history).

Guards: `confirmTenantId` must exactly equal `tenantId`, and `reason` must be at least 10 characters. Protected tenants are rejected with 409.

Returns `{ operationId, tenantId, tenantName, reason, deleted: { users, credentials, lockHolders, lockDefinitions, lockAudit, authSessions, requestHistory, tenant }, startedUtc, completedUtc }`.
